name: Cheilitis glandularis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and histopathological diagnostic criteria for Cheilitis glandularis

criteria.description: Persistent swelling and eversion of the lower lip with visible dilated and inflamed minor salivary gland orifices
Biopsy showing chronic sialadenitis with ductal ectasia, acinar atrophy, and inflammatory infiltrate
Exclusion of other causes of lip inflammation such as actinic cheilitis, contact dermatitis, or infections
Symptoms persisting for months to years despite conservative management

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical presentation plus histopathological confirmation and exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by biopsy; imaging may assist in excluding malignancy.

laboratory: Elevated inflammatory markers may be present in secondary infection
Microbiological cultures from mucopurulent discharge may identify bacterial pathogens
imaging: Ultrasound or MRI may show dilated minor salivary gland ducts and exclude neoplastic lesions
other: Histopathology demonstrating chronic sialadenitis with ductal ectasia and inflammatory infiltrate

distinguishingFeatures: Sun-exposed lip involvement with keratotic changes
Histology showing epithelial dysplasia without glandular inflammation
History of allergen or irritant exposure
Often associated with Candida or bacterial infection

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging lip mass or ulceration suggestive of malignancy
Persistent bleeding or non-healing ulcer on the lip
references: Neville BW, Damm DD, Allen CM, Chi AC. Oral & Maxillofacial Pathology. 4th ed. Elsevier; 2016.
Reichart PA, Philipsen HP. Oral Mucosal Diseases: A Guide to Diagnosis and Management. Springer; 2011.
